recipes.name: Chocolate Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Grease and flour two 9-inch round baking pans.
In a large bowl, stir together the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Add the milk, vegetable oil, eggs, and vanilla to the flour mixture and mix until well combined.
Stir in the boiling water last. The batter will be thin.
Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then remove to a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.name: Belgian Waffles

ingredients.name: toppings: maple syrup, icing sugar, berries, banana, Nutella or whipped cream

instructions: Preheat and grease your waffle iron.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl.
Separate the eggs, making sure no yolk gets into the whites. Whisk the whites with a hand mixer to stiff peaks.
Mix the milk and oil into the yolks, then stir this into the dry ingredients.
Gently fold in the whisked egg whites, without overmixing.
Spoon the batter onto the hot waffle iron and cook according to its instructions until golden.
Serve straight away with your favourite toppings.

recipes.name: Tiramisu (Original Italian Recipe)
instructions: Brew the espresso and let it cool, then stir in the Marsala if using.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, making sure no yolk gets in.
In another bowl, whisk the yolks with the sugar for 3-5 minutes until pale and slightly thick.
Beat in the cold mascarpone until smooth.
Gently fold in the egg whites, lifting from the bottom to keep the cream airy.
Dip each ladyfinger in the coffee for just 1-2 seconds and lay a single layer in your dish.
Spread over half the cream, add a second layer of dipped ladyfingers, then cover with the rest of the cream and smooth the top.
Dust generously with cocoa powder and chill for at least 3 hours, ideally overnight.

recipes.name: Classic British Scones

ingredients.name: clotted cream and jam, to serve

instructions: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan, Gas 7) and line a baking sheet with baking paper.
Sift the flour, salt and sugar into a bowl. Rub in the butter with your fingertips, lifting your hands to add air, until it looks like fine crumbs.
Beat the egg with the buttermilk and stir it in with a round-bladed knife to make a soft, slightly rough dough. Add a little more buttermilk a teaspoon at a time if it's dry.
Tip onto a floured surface, knead very briefly and press out to about 3cm thick.
Stamp out rounds with a floured 6cm cutter, then press the scraps together and cut more.
Space them on the baking sheet, dust lightly with flour and bake for about 12 minutes until deep golden.
Cool slightly on a wire rack and serve warm.

recipes.name: Crispy Waffle Cookies
instructions: Bring the butter and egg to room temperature. You can soften the butter briefly in the microwave, but don't let it melt.
Beat the butter with the sugar until light.
Beat in the egg thoroughly, then add the vanilla.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and fold in with a spatula using a cutting motion, then press it together into a dough.
Heat your waffle maker. Roll small portions of dough into balls and bake them in the waffle maker until golden (about 8-10 per batch on a two-plate machine). Bake longer for crispier cookies.
Leave to cool; they crisp up as they cool.
Variations: add 2 tbsp instant coffee dissolved in 1 tbsp milk before the flour, or ½ tsp cinnamon with the flour, or swap 30g of the flour for ground almonds. Leave out the vanilla for these.

recipes.name: Japanese-Style Belgian Waffles (Yeasted, with Pearl Sugar)

ingredients.name: milk (enough to make the egg and milk 130g together)
pearl sugar, plus extra for sprinkling

instructions: Crack the egg into a jug and top up with milk to 130g in total.
Put everything except the pearl sugar into a bread machine and run the dough cycle.
When the first rise has finished, add the 30g pearl sugar and restart the dough cycle for about 2 minutes, just until it's evenly mixed in. Stop the machine.
Without flouring the surface, divide the sticky dough into 8 pieces, shape loosely into balls and leave to rest.
Meanwhile, preheat the waffle maker (about 5 minutes).
Sprinkle each ball with a little extra pearl sugar if you like, place it in the centre of the waffle plate and bake for about 4-5 minutes. Watch later batches, as they can burn more easily.
Reheat leftovers on a low setting in the toaster to crisp them up again.

recipes.name: Blueberry Baked Cheesecake
instructions: Line a 15-18cm round tin with baking paper and heat the oven to 170C. Make sure the cream cheese and egg are at room temperature.
Crush the biscuits in a sturdy bag with a rolling pin. Melt the butter (30-40 seconds in the microwave) and work it into the crumbs.
Press the crumbs firmly into the base of the tin, cover and chill until firm.
Whisk the cream cheese until smooth (warm it briefly if it's still firm), then mix in the sugar.
Gradually whisk in the egg, then the cream. Sift in the flour and mix until there are no dry streaks.
Stir in the lemon juice, then fold in two-thirds of the frozen blueberries (no need to thaw).
Pour over the base, scatter the rest of the blueberries on top and tap the tin to knock out air bubbles.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden on top. A skewer should come out with moist crumbs but no wet batter.
Cool, then chill for several hours (ideally half a day) before slicing.
